pages.summary: Use this at markets, seafood trays, taxis, and any cash moment where the price needs to be visible before you commit.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Cái này bao nhiêu? is the pointing phrase for one visible thing: a mango, shirt, coffee, seafood tray, menu photo, or ride add-on. The phrase is small, but it protects the moment before money gets awkward.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Keep the item, price tag, calculator, receipt, or ATM screen visible so the reply can be a point, number, or short correction.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Build the line around Cái + này, then replay the full phrase until the rhythm feels natural.

sections.title: Natural variations
sections.body: Use these when the price question needs a softer tone, a total, or a clearer object. The pointing still does most of the work.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: The useful part is timing. Ask before the bag is packed, the plate is weighed, or the ride has started, then repeat or show the number back so both sides see the same price.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: The answer may be spoken fast, typed into a phone, shown on a calculator, or answered with a gesture. If the number matters, ask them to type it.

phrases.english: Can you lower it a little?

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Markets, snack stalls, small shops, beach seafood, laundry counters, and informal rides are where this earns its place. For several items, move to a total-price phrase before paying.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: If the answer comes too fast, hand over your phone calculator or point to theirs. Numbers are easier to trust when both people can see them.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: This phrase names the bag problem before you start explaining. That helps airport staff move straight to the baggage tag, flight details, or next counter. It is more useful than a broad lost-bag sentence when the bag may simply be delayed, still on another carousel, or waiting for a staff handoff.

pages.summary: For asking a driver to slow down when speed, traffic, turns, or rain make the ride uncomfortable.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Say it before the next turn or fast stretch. A small hand-down gesture can help if words are not enough.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say the line once, then pause. If nothing changes, follow with stop at the next corner or drive carefully.

phrases.vietnamese: Xin hãy lái xe chậm lại
phrases.pronunciation: Xin hay lai xe cham lai

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Xin hãy means please; lái xe means drive; chậm lại means slow down.

breakdown.vietnamese: Xin hãy lái xe chậm lại

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Good in taxis, ride-hailing cars, motorbike taxis, vans, and mountain or rainy-road transfers.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: This is more direct than asking if the road is safe. Say it when the speed itself is the problem.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Move to drive-carefully, stop-here, next-corner, follow-map, or wrong-route cards if the ride still needs adjusting.

phrases.english: Please turn on the air conditioning

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: Drive carefully, stop here, next corner, follow the map, and lower the music cards cover the ride adjustment.

examples.vietnamese: Xin hãy lái xe chậm lại
examples.pronunciation: Xin hay lai xe cham lai

pages.title: Hãy đi theo bản đồ
pages.summary: For asking a driver to use the route on your phone.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Useful when the route matters: hotel entrance, pickup lane, toll road, wrong turn, or a specific saved address.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Show the map and say the line before the driver commits to another route.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Hãy đi theo means please follow; bản đồ means map.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Good in taxis, private cars, motorbike taxis, or transfer vans when the map is already open.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Keep your tone practical, not accusatory. Point to the route, not the driver.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Use address, route, wrong way, turn, or stop-here follow-ups if the driver needs the next instruction.

phrases.english: Please turn on the air conditioning

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: If the route still feels wrong, use turn, address, correct street, wrong way, or stop phrases.

pages.title: Hãy đi thẳng
pages.summary: For giving a driver a simple straight-ahead route cue.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use it while the car or bike is moving and the next instruction needs to be short.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say it before the turn decision arrives. Show the map if traffic or lanes make the route unclear.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Hãy is a soft prompt; đi thẳng means go straight.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Good in taxis, motorbike taxis, private cars, hotel-arranged rides, and station pickups.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Short route cues work better before the intersection. A late instruction can sound like a correction.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Use stop-here, turn-right, turn-left, follow-map, aircon, or cash cards if the ride needs another phrase.

phrases.english: Please turn on the air conditioning

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: If the route changes, move to turn-right, turn-left, stop-here, correct-address, or follow-the-map follow-ups.

sections.body: Air-conditioning, bathrooms, snacks, card-friendly shopping, and easy meetups can reset the street plan without sending the group across town.

sections.title: Back To The Center
sections.body: The mall keeps the reset close to the original District 1 plan. When everyone is ready, Dong Khoi, the Opera House area, and the river side of the center are still right outside.

pages.title: Công viên Vinhomes Central Park
pages.summary: The park is an open-air break: riverside paths, lawns, shade, families, evening light, and the Landmark 81 backdrop. Modern Saigon shows up here through lawns, river air, family walks, and Landmark 81 above the park.

cityMetadata.rationale: Modern Saigon shows up here through lawns, river air, family walks, and Landmark 81 above the park.

sections.title: Riverside Space With A Skyline
sections.body: Vinhomes Central Park is a riverside park in Bình Thạnh where lawns, stroller paths, evening walkers, and Landmark 81 share the same view. For someone new to Vietnam, it shows the polished high-rise side of Saigon without leaving the river air.

sections.title: Grass, Strollers, River Air
sections.body: This is open grass, shade, water breaks, kids on paths, and people stretching out after tower or apartment time. Modern Saigon slows down outdoors here.

sections.title: Landmark 81 Above The Park
sections.body: The tower rises above the lawns, so photos and directions often orbit around it. Look back from the paths and the park reads as Bình Thạnh skyline, not market-street Saigon.

sections.title: Evening By The River
sections.body: At dusk, the lawns fill with families, walkers, cooler air, and tower light. The river edge gives the evening a little room after traffic and indoor time.

sections.title: After Museums And Markets
sections.body: After dense museum rooms or market streets, this is the other side of the city: high-rises, grass, river wind, and a place to walk without buying anything.

pages.title: Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh
pages.pronunciation: bow tahng chung tich chien tranh
pages.summary: War Remnants Museum changes the day from restaurants, streets, and skyline into recent history. It is a serious museum visit. The museum is a sobering historical room, with a weight that changes the pace of the day.

cityMetadata.rationale: The museum is a sobering historical room, with a weight that changes the pace of the day.

sections.title: A Serious War History Visit
sections.body: War Remnants Museum is Saigon's serious museum about the Vietnam War, told through photographs, documents, military equipment, and prison-related exhibits. Give the day room for the material instead of squeezing it between errands.

sections.title: Photographs Set The Pace
sections.body: The photo rooms ask for slower reading than a normal museum walk. Documents, images, and captions carry much of the weight before the outdoor military equipment comes back into view.

sections.title: Leave Room Afterward
sections.body: After the exhibits, a shaded walk, simple meal, or low-key cafe gives the visit room to settle. The material is hard to carry straight into the next loud plan.

sections.title: Images Stay With You
sections.body: Some rooms are graphic and direct. Move through the photos and captions at a pace the group can absorb before heading upstairs or outside.

sections.title: Famous, Still Sober
sections.body: The museum is well known, but the subject does not become lighter because it is famous. Expect a sober visit with history in the rooms, the courtyard, and the conversation afterward.

pages.title: The Workshop Coffee

cityMetadata.rationale: Saigon has many quick coffee stops; The Workshop gives the coffee scene a more deliberate specialty-cafe version above the street.

sections.title: A Coffee Break Above The Street
sections.body: The Workshop Coffee is an upstairs specialty cafe in central Saigon, with espresso gear, pour-over pacing, and tables above the street. The climb changes the coffee moment from sidewalk speed to a room where the cup gets time.

sections.title: Gear On The Counter
sections.body: Beans, grinders, espresso gear, and pour-over setup sit in view. Ordering here is closer to choosing a brew than grabbing a quick iced glass between errands.

sections.title: Upstairs From The Noise
sections.body: The stairs pull you out of traffic and into an older central building. Counter seats, tables, and street views put one full floor between you and the motorbike noise below.

sections.title: Between Heat And Meals
sections.body: Between market walking, lunch, and evening plans, caffeine plus a real chair can reset the next stretch. It is a good room for choosing the next address before going back outside.

sections.title: Saigon Coffee, Slowed Down
sections.body: The city has fast sidewalk coffee everywhere. This room gives the same coffee appetite a slower specialty version, with beans, timing, and brew method doing more of the talking.

pages.title: Thảo Cầm Viên Sài Gòn
pages.summary: The visit is about space and age: old trees, paths, shade, families, open lawns, and a city institution near the center. Central Saigon has a long green institution here, with the zoo and gardens sitting inside everyday family movement.

cityMetadata.rationale: Central Saigon has a long green institution here, with the zoo and gardens sitting inside everyday family movement.

sections.title: Old Trees Inside The City
sections.body: Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens is an open-air city park with old trees, walking paths, gardens, and animal areas. Plan for shade, water, and a slower pace.

sections.title: Paths Under Old Trees
sections.body: The grounds spread out under old trees, with paths that turn the visit into a slow outdoor walk. The animal areas sit inside that larger park rhythm.

sections.title: Gardens Between Enclosures
sections.body: Gardens, benches, tree canopy, and winding paths give the visit breathing room between animal areas. Shade and water breaks are part of the rhythm from the start.

sections.title: Family-Day Rhythm
sections.body: Families, slow walking, snack breaks, and shaded benches give the zoo its everyday Saigon rhythm. It reads more like a local day out than a polished tourist attraction.

sections.title: Plan Around Shade
sections.body: On a hot day, the shade changes the whole visit. Walk a section, rest under trees, check water, then move to the next animal area.

pages.title: Cầu Rồng ở đâu?
pages.summary: For making the sightseeing or ticket question clear at a ticket desk, tour counter, entrance, or meeting point while the ticket, booking, meeting point, map location, or attraction name stays visible.

editorialSupportMetadata.rationale: Required by EP-006 because the pilot visible row needs the exact Dragon Bridge where-question.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: This is the simple location question for finding Dragon Bridge when it is close in the plan but not obvious on the street.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say it while showing the map or place card. The question asks for orientation, not a ride or exact curb.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Cầu Rồng is the map location. Ở đâu asks where, so the whole line is a compact landmark-location question.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it with hotel staff, a driver, a guard, or someone nearby when pointing at the map is not enough.

phrases.vietnamese: Bạn chụp giúp tôi được không?
phrases.english: Can you take a photo for me?
phrases.pronunciation: ban choop zoop toy duoc khong

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: If someone points across the river or names a side, keep the map visible and confirm the next walking step.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Go next to drop-off, take-me-there, photo, and taxi-return phrases.

sections.title: Near the landmark
sections.body: Use it before a photo stop, river walk, taxi drop-off, or handoff where Dragon Bridge is the reference point.

pages.title: Tài xế chờ ở đâu?
pages.summary: For making the ride or fare need clear during a taxi ride, motorbike pickup, or station-counter exchange while the destination, fare, or ride screen stays visible.

editorialSupportMetadata.rationale: Required by EP-007 as stable visitor-flow support for Marble Mountains without importing time-sensitive policy claims.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: This supports attraction pages where the visit has an entrance and a return point. It avoids assuming any current pickup policy.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Ask it before you go inside or up stairs. The answer may be a gate, parking area, or pointed direction.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Tài xế is driver, chờ is wait, and ở đâu asks where. Together they solve the return-point problem.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it before attractions with entrances, stairs, caves, pagodas, or large grounds where the pickup point matters.

sections.title: Good to know

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: This phrase keeps the dish page local to Hoi An by asking someone nearby for a practical food pointer.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Ask it at a hotel desk, cafe, or shop when you want a simple recommendation or direction.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The frame ở đâu có asks where there is something. Ngon asks for a good-tasting option without claiming a ranking.

breakdown.vietnamese: Ở đâu có cao lầu ngon?

sections.title: When to use it

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: This asks for local help, not a verified ranking. If the answer is a name, show your map and ask them to point.

pages.title: Chùa Linh Ứng ở đâu?
pages.summary: For making the sightseeing or ticket question clear at a ticket desk, tour counter, entrance, or meeting point while the ticket, booking, meeting point, map location, or attraction name stays visible.

editorialSupportMetadata.rationale: Required by EP-008 because the pilot visible row names Linh Ung Pagoda as the specific stop.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Chùa Linh Ứng ở đâu? belongs at a ticket desk, tour counter, entrance, or meeting point when the ticket, booking, meeting point, map location, or attraction name is already part of the exchange.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say it with the place card visible. The question is useful at a curb, parking area, hotel desk, or viewpoint turnoff.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Chùa Linh Ứng is the pagoda name. Ở đâu asks where it is.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it when a driver, guard, or helper can point you toward the pagoda entrance or next turn.

phrases.english: What time do we come back?

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: If someone answers with a gesture, follow by showing the map location and asking for the next walking step.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Go next to Sơn Trà route, wait-here, return-time, and photo phrases.
